reports.title: Anthony Binfield, David Richards and Rolandas Karbauskas: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

promises.quote: The Trust has established enhanced Executive led oversight and assurance reviews for Offender Health. This comprises a weekly meeting where progress against the Transformation Plan is reviewed with individuals held to account.
promises.summary: Establish weekly executive oversight of offender health transformation plan

promises.quote: A new national template for prison reception screening for the male prison estate was launched on the 1 April 2025. Staff are in the process of receiving the Nationally delivered Highbury Hospital, Highbury Road, Nottingham, NG6 9DR training for this and the benefits include a standardised and simplified model of screening which enable the understanding and recording of previously documented clinical risk which needs to be further considered as part of the reception and induction process.
promises.summary: Implement new reception screening template and training

promises.quote: The Head of Safer Custody has introduced a new Early Days in Custody (EDIC) booklet along with colleagues from Reception and the Induction wing.
promises.summary: Introduce EDIC booklet for immediate risk identification

promises.quote: We have worked with Prison colleagues to ensure that SIMs are attended on a weekly basis by a member of the Mental Health Team. This meeting is to discuss any patients of concern and highlight any specific issues relating to that individual.
promises.summary: Ensure weekly SIM attendance by mental health staff

promises.quote: CSIP: Patients can also be referred to CSIP (Challenge, Support and Intervention Plan). This is a prison risk management system and process that will enable information sharing on risk in the prison estate and also support the development of cross professional relationships. Healthcare staff are currently accessing the training for this, and full compliance is aimed to have been achieved by June 2025.

Training - Healthcare staff have arranged to attend the Prison staff induction programme so that they can deliver health training to the Prison Officers. Initially this will be focused on emergency response but will later include Mental Health awareness training. This was agreed at the Local Delivery Board and the first session was provided on 23 January 2025. Feedback from staff was very positive. promises.summary: Provide mental health awareness training to prison staff

promises.quote: Failure to identify and share risk pertinent information between prison and healthcare staff.
promises.summary: Improve risk information sharing between prison and healthcare staff.
